quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
rationale: Section 15.1 gives us a vendor-side indemnity from MSL covering (a) third-party IP infringement (patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work, trade secret) arising from MSL's performance, procured Parts, processes, designs, deliverables or pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with law, and (c) failure to perform its warranty/support obligations — the core of the preferred position. Exclusions are the usual ones (IBM-selected marks, IBM written specifications, IBM-provided defective designs), and Section 15.2 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control with our right to participate at our expense) plus procure/redesign remedies at MSL's expense. There is no reciprocal IBM indemnity of MSL anywhere in the Agreement, and Appendix A §5 adds a further MSL indemnity for Microsoft code, so the allocation runs in our favour. Minor points noted but not flagged: the indemnity names IBM rather than IBM and its affiliates, and does not separately call out data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; also, the mutual 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap in Section 15.3(b) would on its face apply to indemnity recoveries — that cap is properly addressed under the limitation-of-liability rule rather than double-flagged here.

quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position and runs in our favour throughout. Section 13.1 (p0197) has MSL assign to IBM all intellectual and industrial property rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered, and p0198 extends IBM ownership (with MSL assignment) to any invention MSL makes on Products or on IBM processes and systems, with MSL only retaining a use right for performing its obligations here — i.e. deliverables and work product vest in us with no joint ownership. Section 13.3(a) (p0208) expressly protects our pre-existing IP: nothing grants MSL any rights or licences in IBM's pre-existing IP except a royalty-free licence to use IBM confidential information under the AECI solely to manufacture Products for IBM, with any further licence requiring a separate signed agreement. Confidential information disclosed to MSL is returnable on demand (13.2(c)), and under the Loan Agreement Section 5 (p1530) IBM retains title to all Loaned Items with no transfer rights for MSL. On tooling, SOW 21.1(e) (p1105) confirms all tools, dies, jigs, patterns, equipment or Parts purchased, furnished, charged to or paid for by IBM become and remain IBM property; MSL's ownership of generic "Common Tooling" (p1088) is precisely the vendor-tools carve-out the playbook accepts. No provision assigns IBM IP, data or classified parts information to MSL, and there is no joint ownership. Two minor sub-elements worth noting but not flagging: there is no express licence-back of MSL background IP embedded in Products (mitigated by the breadth of the 13.1 assignment plus the bar on MSL using proprietary assembly/test processes), and there is no standalone "Customer Data" ownership sentence, which is unsurprising in a 1998 manufacturing outsourcing deal where information flows are governed by the AECI.

quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement grants or may grant MSL any rights or licenses in any preexisting intellectual property of IBM except that IBM grants MSL a royalty-free license to use the confidential information disclosed in connection with this Agreement under the AECI referenced in 13.2 necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM.
rationale: Every licence grant in this agreement runs from us (IBM) to the counterparty (MSL), not the reverse: §13.3(a) gives MSL only a narrow royalty-free right to use IBM confidential information to manufacture Products solely for IBM; §24.1(a) and the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §§5-6 likewise grant MSL limited, use-restricted rights in IBM software, Loaned Programs and Licensed Internal Code. Those restrictions benefit our side and are not flagged. Our own position is stronger than the preferred licence position rather than weaker: under §13.1 IBM "assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products", plus assignment of MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes, and MSL is barred from using proprietary processes for the Products absent written agreement — so we hold ownership rather than a revocable licence, and there is no grant to us that MSL can revoke at will or that excludes our affiliates or contractors. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording but are noted only: the agreement contains no IBM affiliate/"Related Company" extension (the concept is used only for MSL) and no express licence-back of MSL background IP for transition to a replacement manufacturer; successor/assignment mechanics sit in §16.2 and §16.5 (with MSL warranting that any acquirer assumes performance) and are addressed under the assignment rule rather than double-flagged here.

quote: Nothing in this Agreement authorizes MSL to use any of IBM's tangible, real or intangible property for the performance of any services contemplated hereunder on IBM Logo products or for Integration services of non-IBM Logo products related to a customer for whom Integration is being provided by IBM.

The restriction-flavoured provisions all run the other way and are therefore acceptable: § 14.18 limits MSL's use of IBM property and MSL's competing Integration activity, and § 16.15 (Prohibited Suppliers) constrains MSL's sourcing. §§ 3.0 and 11.0 are scope-of-work only and contain no requirements/sole-source commitment obliging IBM to buy exclusively from MSL, so our freedom to build in-house or dual-source is unimpaired. The confidentiality carve-out at p1490–1491 affirmatively preserves each Recipient's right to provide products or services competitive with the Discloser's and to supply the Discloser's competitors, which benefits us. § 5.1(v) is a change-of-control termination trigger rather than a covenant. Noted but not flagged under this rule: § 9.0(f) binds IBM not to solicit Transferred Employees for a stated period, but that is a personnel non-solicit (time-limited, with inbound-applicant and general-advertising carve-outs), not a restriction on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build; it belongs to any non-solicitation rule rather than this one. quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (Section 4.0; mirrored in SOW Section 2.0) and Section 5.0 permits termination only "for cause" — material breach, insolvency events, change of control or force majeure (Section 5.1 a)–c)). There is no right for IBM to terminate for convenience at any point during the multi-year term; the only no-cause exit is a six-month (twelve-month under the SOW) non-renewal notice that bites only at the end of a term. That fails both the preferred position (30 days' notice) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped early-termination fee), and sits in walk-away territory ("no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term"). The PO-level cancellation right in SOW Section 6.1 lets us cancel individual Purchase Orders but does not give an agreement-level exit and is expressly subject to cost reimbursements, so it does not cure the gap. On the other side of the ledger the position is acceptable: MSL likewise has no mid-term convenience right and any non-renewal requires at least six months' notice, so no vendor-side redline is needed. We have therefore added a new Section 5.4 giving IBM a 30-day convenience right with a refund of prepayments, while preserving MSL's payment entitlements under Sections 5.2 and 5.3 and confirming MSL has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

verification.notes: Deviation classification is supported: the cited text commits IBM to a three-year term with automatic renewal (p0104/p0658) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause, so there is no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term — squarely the rule's walk-away scenario, failing both preferred (30 days) and fallback (60–90 days with capped fee). The rationale correctly disposes of the near-miss alternatives (six/twelve-month non-renewal notice bites only at term end; SOW 6.1 PO cancellation is order-level and cost-reimbursable), so this is not an acceptable-fallback clause being over-upgraded. The inserted language reaches the preferred position with a targeted addition: 30 days' written notice, no termination penalty, refund of prepaid amounts, and an express bar on MSL terminating for convenience mid-term; it is an insert rather than a rewrite, so no unnecessary disturbance of surrounding text. The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a phrasing artifact ('for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice') rather than a substantive gap — the Customer convenience right is plainly granted. Carve-out for amounts payable under Sections 5.2/5.3 is a reasonable manufacturing-inventory concession (payment for goods, not an early-termination penalty) and does not fall below the fallback; the comment accurately describes the change and cites the playbook position. Minor nit only (not a fail): the inserted clause is described as 'Section 5.4' in the rationale but the rendered text carries no section number, so the numbering should be added on execution.

quote: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable.
rationale: There is no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment on us. § 6.0 obliges us to purchase only Products we order ("This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product"), and § 6.1 lets us cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time, so fees follow ordered volumes only — the preferred position. Our residual volume-related exposure is expressly limited: § 13.2(e) states "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility"; § 13.3(b) leaves EOL inventory not transferred as MSL's sole responsibility; and § 13.0(f) confirms we have no liability for inventory MSL purchases so long as forecast accuracy meets the Appendix 2 level. The only payment obligation tied to volumes is the Appendix 2 requirements-accuracy compensation (a defined percentage of material cost payable if our forecast accuracy falls below the stated threshold), which operates as a forecast true-up compensating MSL for material it bought against our forecast rather than a shortfall penalty or multi-year take-or-pay; it is quantified, quarterly and self-liquidating. Noted for the record but not a deviation: the true-up has no aggregate cap, which we would only pursue if reopening the pricing appendices.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected posture; nothing is being raised against the counterparty. No take-or-pay, minimum volume, or shortfall penalty language appears in the cited paragraphs; volume-related exposure is expressly limited (p0927 'IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility'; p0930 EOL inventory remains MSL's sole responsibility; p0903 no liability for MSL-purchased inventory subject to forecast accuracy). The Appendix 2 requirements-accuracy compensation is correctly characterized as a quantified, quarterly forecast true-up (percentage of material cost of volume shipped) rather than a multi-year shortfall penalty, so it sits within the rule's fallback/true-up concept at worst; the uncapped nature is properly noted in the rationale rather than flagged as a deviation. quote: f) IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date of this Agreement, it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees without the prior written consent of MSL; provided, however, that the foregoing will not restrict or prevent IBM from a) employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM or b) by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto
rationale: Section 9.0(f) is the only hiring restriction in the Agreement (16.7 and 5.2 contain no personnel-hiring constraints), and it binds IBM. It sits at the playbook fallback on all material terms: (i) scope is narrow — limited to the finite, listed group of "Transferred Employees" (the ex-IBM staff who moved to MSL to perform the work), not all MSL personnel; (ii) it is a solicitation-only restriction with no "no-hire" — IBM may in fact hire Transferred Employees who approach it or respond to advertising; and (iii) both required carve-outs are present, for unsolicited approaches on the individual's own initiative and for general employment advertising/communications and independent search firms. Two points short of the preferred position are noted rather than flagged: the covenant is one-way rather than mutual, and the duration is redacted ("[*] years") and runs from the Effective Date rather than from the end of an individual's involvement. We should confirm on the unredacted copy that the period does not exceed 24 months (walk-away); as drafted from a fixed Effective Date rather than a rolling engagement date, the restriction is self-limiting and does not warrant a redline.

This is a manufacturing/Products deal, so the absence of a separate professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, compliance-with-laws warranty and malicious-code warranty is immaterial here, and the warranty exclusions in 19.1(a)(ii)-(iii) relate to IBM Parts and consigned Products (our own materials) and 19.3 to misuse, both customary. ops.text:
16.22 Insurance

MSL shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than U.S. $1,000,000 per occurrence and U.S. $2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than U.S. $2,000,000; (c) where MSL processes, stores or has access to IBM or IBM customer data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than U.S. $5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation and employer's liability insurance as required by applicable law. Such coverage is in addition to the replacement value insurance for consigned Products required under the Statement of Work. MSL shall provide IBM with certificates of insurance upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 16.22 requiring MSL to carry commercial general liability, professional liability, cyber and workers' compensation insurance, with certificates on request.

quote: MSL will provide replacement value insurance coverage for consigned Products. IBM will be named as a joint insured with respect to consigned Products for its interest.
rationale: The Agreement contains no vendor insurance covenant. The only insurance references are narrow and property-specific: SOW 13.1(b) requires MSL to carry replacement-value cover for IBM consigned Products (with IBM as joint insured); SOW 21.2 obliges IBM (not MSL) to insure IBM-owned tooling; Loan Agreement Section 8 relieves MSL of risk of loss on Loaned Items; and 10.0 defers premises terms to a separate Lease of Premises Agreement not before us. None of these provide commercial general liability, professional liability (E&O), cyber/privacy or workers' compensation cover, so the document fails even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). This matters here because MSL occupies IBM premises, holds IBM and IBM-customer consigned inventory, and accesses IBM applications, networks and customer integration data under SOW 24.1 — squarely the exposure the rule targets. Redline inserts a new Section 16.22 in the General section at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), expressly preserving the existing consigned-Products cover, with the fallback limits offered in the comment.

verification.notes: Directionally correct for us as the customer (IBM): the inserted covenant imposes insurance obligations on the vendor (MSL) and does not create risk for our side. 'Missing' status is supported — the only insurance references in the document are narrow property covers (replacement value for consigned Products, IBM-owned tooling insured by IBM, risk-of-loss relief on Loaned Items), none of which reach CGL, E&O, cyber or workers' compensation, so the clause set fails even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). The rule's trigger is met on the facts cited: MSL occupies IBM premises, holds IBM and IBM-customer consigned inventory, and accesses IBM systems/customer data. Redline tracks the model language closely (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request, survival for one year) and sensibly preserves the existing consigned-Products cover rather than displacing it — minimal, self-contained insertion. Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states the playbook position and offers the fallback limits; deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present. Minor, non-fatal: the insertion is anchored after an infringement/suspension remedy paragraph rather than clearly at the end of the General section — the new '16.22' heading should be confirmed against the actual General section numbering before sending.
